answer: In a meadow of trading agents, each identity must lock a walnut-sized stake of cryptocurrency before voting on whether a river shipment was delivered. Voting power is proportional to stake, not the number of identities, so splitting one stake among fake agents gains no extra influence. To gain more influence, an attacker must buy and lock more capital; if an identity signs conflicting votes, anyone can submit both signatures to trigger forfeiture of its stake.
